Enjoy this exciting Level 1 Scholastic Reader from the bestselling author of Who Would Win?"-- Provided by publisher.

summary: "Two young friends search for the endangered tiger in the latest in this picture-book series. Animal expert Alex wants to help her friend Atticus spot a tiger. Sharing cool tiger facts from her journal, she shows Atticus what to look for. Each new fact leads Atticus to think he sees the elusive beasts everywhere: This critter has stripes and that one has enormous teeth. Young readers will love knowing more than Atticus, as his confident refrain "Is this a tiger?" invites a resounding "NO!" Spreads shown from Alex's field guide are lined with tiger facts. The back matter includes further information about tigers and bonus facts about the other animals that appear in the book"--Provided by publisher.

summary: Super Facts for Super Kids is a fun and fresh take on nonfiction for beginning readers. Filled with engaging photographs, comic-style illustrations, and cool infographics, this Level 2 Ready-to-Read series about animals is sure to flip, float, and fly off the shelves.  What makes tigers terrific? Tigers are the largest cats in the world, but did you know that they can't purr? They also like swimming to cool down on hot days! Readers will love learning about tigers, from their unique stripes to their sharp claws in this book that presents information in a highly visual way for young readers. A special section in the back discusses the tiger's endangered status and the importance of jungle conservation.

summary: Tiger is in a terrible mood. He has been angry with everyone all day. Then Monkey accidentally chooses the book that Tiger wanted and Tiger has a tantrum in the library. How can Miss Bird help Tiger to manage his anger, and how can he make up with his friends? A lively board book that examines feelings of anger in an amusing but reassuring way through animal characters - perfect for young children who are experiencing angry emotions. The story offers a gentle way in to discuss this difficult emotion.

Tiger is in a terrible mood. He has been angry with everyone all day. Then Monkey accidentally chooses the book that Tiger wanted and Tiger has a full blown tantrum in the library. How can Miss Bird help Tiger to manage his anger, and how can he make up with his friends? This series introduces children to different emotions and behaviour. A fun story featuring fantastic characters is backed up by suggestions for activities and ideas to talk through together.

It's never nice to throw a tantrum, not even if you're a tiger! Through this charming fictional story, readers learn how to handle anger in a healthy way. Accessible text allows readers to explore important character-building concepts, including understanding emotions and owning up to bad behavior. Colorful illustrations add fun details to this engaging story. Detailed follow-up questions are included to facilitate helpful discussions after reading. What are better ways than throwing a tantrum to deal with angry feelings? Tiger will help readers find the answer!

"In Tiger Cubs in the Wild, beginning readers will learn about baby tigers as they grow up in the rain forest in Asia. Follow along as tiger cubs learn from their moms. Vibrant, full-color photos and carefully leveled text will engage young readers as they are introduced to tiger cubs' appearance, diet, behaviors, and habitat. A picture diagram labels a tiger cub's body parts, while a picture glossary reinforces new vocabulary. Children can learn more about tiger cubs online using our safe search engine that provides relevant, age-appropriate websites. Tiger Cubs in the Wild also features reading tips for teachers and parents, a table of contents, and an index. Tiger Cubs in the Wild is part of Jump!'s Baby Animals in the Wild! series"--Provided by publisher.
